entries.core_move: Determine whether a continuous-time signal is bounded by identifying a finite magnitude limit over all time for use in BIBO stability reasoning.
Apply the BIBO stability criterion by checking whether every bounded continuous-time input necessarily produces a bounded output under a given system rule.
Interpret a stable physical continuous-time system as one whose response remains finite because its dynamics prevent bounded inputs from accumulating without bound.

Relate damping and dissipation mechanisms in continuous-time physical systems to decaying responses that support BIBO stability by preventing bounded inputs from accumulating into growing or unbounded outputs.
Classify unstable continuous-time systems by applying the BIBO criterion to recognize bounded inputs that produce unbounded output growth due to insufficient damping or reinforcing dynamics.
Classify integrator-type systems by testing whether their cumulative input-output rule can turn a bounded input into an unbounded output under the BIBO stability criterion.
Disprove BIBO stability for a continuous-time system by tracing a bounded input through the system rule and demonstrating that the resulting output has no finite bound.
Classify continuous-time system examples as BIBO stable or unstable by identifying whether bounded inputs produce bounded outputs or reveal growth, inadequate damping, or integrator accumulation.
